preview_en:
The final La Liga game before the international break sees a refreshed Valencia looking to make up lost ground against a Real Sociedad side who’ve endured a turbulent week.

Match News and Current Form

Valencia’s decision to sack Carlos Corberán just five rounds into the new season paid off in the immediate short term, as Óscar Sánchez became the club’s first head coach since Gennaro Gattuso in 2022 to win their debut game in charge. The breakthrough 1-0 win at Alavés only saw Los Che match their worst start to a La Liga campaign at this stage this century, and wasn’t enough to lift them out of the relegation zone. Home improvements could be the route to safety for Valencia here given that they’ve so far failed to score at the Mestalla this season (D1, L2).

Pellegrino Matarazzo’s Real Sociedad couldn't repeat their famous Copa Del Rey final victory over Atlético Madrid last Sunday, being humbled 3-0 before losing 2-1 to Bournemouth in their UEFA Europa League opener on Thursday. La Real now look to respond, and though they languish in mid-table, they’ll be quick to point out that their three La Liga defeats came against sides in the pre-round top four. Sociedad also boast a better points tally at this stage than the previous two seasons, but building on that looks tricky for a side who’ve won once on the road in La Liga since the start of March (D3, L5).

Head-to-Head History

Valencia are looking to record consecutive wins over Sociedad for the first time since 2018 after winning 4-3 in the most recent H2H. They’ve lost only one of their last nine games at home to Sociedad (W3, D5).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Valencia are yet to lead a La Liga game at half-time this season (HT: D4, L2).

Valencia were held scoreless in five of their last six league losses.

Eleven of Sociedad’s last 14 away league games saw both teams score.

Sociedad haven't trailed at half-time in La Liga this season (HT: W1, D5).

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Javi Guerra is unbeaten when scoring for Valencia in La Liga (W9, D2). Five of his last seven league strikes came at home, with the two exceptions scored against Sociedad! A scorer of 36 goals in 178 appearances for Valencia, Sociedad’s Gonçalo Guedes looks to open his account for the season in familiar surroundings with six of his nine strikes for La Real coming after half-time.

Cesar Tarrega , Mouctar Diakhaby , Luis Rioja and Umar Sadiq are all doubts for Valencia. Sociedad’s Igor Zubeldia could return after two games out.
